source.section: Form NJ-1040 lines 15, 20a, 27, 28a, 29: Instr PDF p.10 exempt income ('Railroad Retirement (Tier 1 and Tier 2)'), PDF p.15 line 20a nontaxable list, PDF p.22 line 28a (Line A, Line B and chart), PDF p.22 line 28b and PDF p.23 Worksheet D lines 1-9 with the Maximum Exclusion chart, PDF p.22 line 29; PDF p.8 lines 6-7 (regular and senior 65+ exemptions), PDF p.9 line 13, PDF p.25 line 30, PDF p.27 lines 38-39, PDF p.33 lines 42-43, PDF p.65 Tax Rate Schedules

worked: Federal AGI 94,000.00 (wages 40,000.00 + Railroad Retirement Tier 2 (taxed federally as a pension) 24,000.00 + private pension 30,000.00); federal taxable income = 94,000.00 - 17,750.00 federal standard deduction (15,750 single + 2,000 for age 65 or older) = 76,250.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Railroad Retirement (Tier 1 and Tier 2) is exempt and not reported. Line 15 wages 40,000.00 + line 20a private pension 30,000.00 = line 27 total income 70,000.00. The projection's income test measure is federal AGI less taxable Social Security = 94,000.00 (it still holds the 24,000 Railroad Retirement, which line 27 does not); both are in the 0-100,000 band (keep share 1). Line 28a: age 67; Line A 30,000.00 (Railroad Retirement is not on line 20a), Line B 75,000.00; lesser = 30,000.00. Line 28b: wages 40,000 over 3,000, so none; projection 0.00 (no covered interest, dividends or gains). Line 29 New Jersey gross income = 70,000.00 - 30,000.00 - 0.00 = 40,000.00. Line 30 exemptions (line 13): regular 1,000 x 1 + senior 65+ 1,000 x 1 = 2,000.00; line 38 = 2,000.00 (no other deductions). Line 39/42 taxable income = 40,000.00 - 2,000.00 = 38,000.00. Line 43 tax, rate schedule Table A (single/separate) as bands: 20,000.00 x 0.014 = 280.00 + 15,000.00 x 0.0175 = 262.50 + 3,000.00 x 0.035 = 105.00 = 647.50. The booklet's Tax Table (taxable income under 100,000) gives 648 for the 38,000-38,050 row (schedule at the midpoint 38,025, rounded); expected keeps the exact schedule result. No credits. State income tax = 647.50. The pension is noncontributory, so the New Jersey taxable amount (line 20a) equals the federal taxable amount and line 20b is empty.
accepted_approximations: Income test measure: line 27 total income is mapped to federal AGI less taxable Social Security plus tax-exempt interest (other states' bonds are taxable in New Jersey and count in line 27; New Jersey bonds and Treasury interest do not count, which the projection can't tell apart).
Tax Table: for taxable income under 100,000 New Jersey uses its Tax Table, the schedule's tax at each 50-dollar row's midpoint rounded to the dollar; the projection uses the exact schedule.
